prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best parent c021 (decay<=0.5, ignore_net_degree halved, adam scheme) is robust; combining it with a modest, bounded per-net weight cap applied only to the effective weight passed to the C++ update (via the existing `max_net_weight` argument) will spread timing weight across more moderately-critical nets and reduce TNS without the systematic failures seen when the cap was set too tight externally.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.773 robust(mean-std)=+0.219 min_case=+0.219 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.219 dWNS=+28.0% dTNS=+17.5% overflow~123
  bp-ng45: score=+0.311 dWNS=+31.8% dTNS=+30.7% overflow~100
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.244 dWNS=+27.5% dTNS=+22.3% overflow~139
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: the bounded per-net cap improved all three cases with no invalid runs. dWNS rose 27.5–31.8% and dTNS 17.5–30.7%, with overflow ~100–139. The mechanism is plausible—capping effective weight spreads timing pressure to moderately-critical nets, reducing TNS without the systematic failures of a tight external cap. Next step: sweep the cap value (e.g., 0.5×, 1×, 2× current) to confirm the bounded region is robust and locate the onset of the earlier failure mode.
